label: Transaction Details
title: Transaction Details
summary: Use Transaction Details to list the facts of one payment as label and value pairs: its ID, the accounts, and how it was paid.
corePrinciple: Name the fact, then give it.

anatomy.title: Labels over values
anatomy.description: Each item puts a label over its value, and the list stacks the items 16 px apart. There’s no surface, divider, or icon: the screen around it provides those.

configuration.title: Only the items
configuration.description: The list has nothing to set: no variants, and no mode changes it. You choose the items and their order, one TransactionDetails.Item each, with a label and a value. Put the reference people quote first, then who paid whom, then how.
blocks: The ID, both ends, then the method.

states.title: Static text
states.description: The list has no states: its items don’t press, select, copy, collapse, or page. To let people copy an ID or share the receipt, put a button on the screen.

sizing.title: As wide as its column
sizing.description: The list has no width of its own: it fills its column, and each item is as wide as its text. A long value wraps under its label; nothing is cut. Figma draws the items at a fixed 315 px. Items sit 16 px apart, and a label sits 4 px above its value, each on a 17 px line.

content.title: Field names and data
content.description: Write each label as a field name, such as UPI transaction ID, From, To, or Payment method. Write the value as the data itself, never a sentence, and mask account numbers to their last four digits. The label shouldn’t repeat the value.

inContext.title: The receipt behind a payment
inContext.description: The details sit on the screen a payment opens, under its amount and outcome. The screen adds the heading and the action; the list only holds the facts, and its accessibilityLabel, Payment details, names it for screen readers.

sources.title: Use the public Transaction Details contract
sources.description: The guide compares the Figma component with the installed package and its Storybook stories.
blocks: Installed jfs-components is 0.1.78 (27 October build of Biscuit’s main) from the team’s private package repository. Figma’s Transaction Details is one component with no properties: a slot of Detail Items, each with a Label and a Value, drawn 315 px wide. The package takes TransactionDetails.Item children with label and value and sizes them to their text. No mode changes it. On the web it’s a list named by its accessibilityLabel, and each item is read once as its label and value, unless the item’s own accessibilityLabel replaces them; phone screen readers read the items too.
